payload.summary: Catalogue search trips its 1,200 ms budget on the FIRST read after an idle period; warm reads are well inside it, and the render_payload waste is real but is not the trigger
payload.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-21, and this row exists because two earlier diagnoses of the same symptom were both wrong. THE SYMPTOM. The 6-hourly Live domain monitor failed 7 of its last 8 runs from 2026-09-18. Every other probe is green; only catalogue search fails, for forms, services and medications, and it flips between probes minutes apart. The app's own Railway log gives the mechanism: 'Canonical catalogue read failed; search is serving in-bundle seeds', catalogue_kind=form, failure=TimeoutError, detail='Canonical form read exceeded 1200ms.', budget_ms=1200, cooldown_ms=30000, with the recovery line 29 s later. NOT THE QUERY, which disproves the mechanism #PX8N86 states and that b8abcd96 carries forward. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) on production: read_site_content_public_records returns 227 service rows in 21.4 ms and 330 medication rows in 22.2 ms - that kind's rows only, not all 843. The kind filter reaches the scan; migration 20260916103000 did that. A stored indexed kind column would not help, because there is nothing left for it to fix. NOT THE PAYLOAD EITHER, which disproves this row's own first draft. Calling the same PostgREST RPC the app calls, warm: form 996 kB in 216 ms, differential 1.47 MB in 264 ms, service 2.64 MB in 396 ms, medication 4.66 MB in 604 ms. Cost does scale with bytes at roughly 13-20 ms per 100 kB, but every warm read finishes far inside 1,200 ms even at 4.66 MB. IT IS THE FIRST CALL. The first read in a fresh process cost 1,781 ms (TTFB 1,599 ms) - over budget on its own. CONTROL: re-running with the order reversed moved the penalty with the position, not the kind - medication first cost 1,268 ms while form, now last, cost 213 ms. So whichever kind is read first after an idle period pays roughly 1.3-1.8 s of connection setup and blows the budget; the 30 s cooldown then holds that kind degraded. The monitor runs 6-hourly against an app that is otherwise idle, which is why it sees a failure most runs while interactive probing finds the site healthy. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX. Shrinking the search read is still worth doing as efficiency - render_payload is 56-64 percent of every read (medications 1,028 kB record vs 1,419 kB render_payload; services 428 vs 552; differentials 336 vs 426; forms 146 vs 257) - but it must NOT drop fields search needs. universal-search.ts calls readCanonicalSiteContentRecords without mapRecord, and that helper returns row.render_payload in that case; the catalogue rankers expect medication/service/form fields from it. Any search-scoped projection has to keep those render fields. A blanket 'payload unused on read' claim is wrong. And even a correct shrink would NOT fix this row, because warm reads are already inside budget and the cold first call is the miss. Ship projection work as efficiency, never as the remedy for this row. SUGGESTED FIX, in order: keep the connection warm or pre-warm on boot so no user-facing read is ever the first; or retry once before falling back, since the second call is warm; or raise the budget for the first call only. Any of those is app-side and needs no migration. Do not simply raise budget_ms globally - that greens the monitor and deletes the only signal that says a cold read takes 1.8 s. EVIDENCE NOTE. Sentry carries these events (JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-2Z, 20 occurrences, mechanism auto.db.supabase.postgres, last seen at exactly the failing monitor's timestamp) but records only 'Unhandled server request error' with no Postgres detail. Sentry alone cannot diagnose this; the Railway deployment log line is the one that can.
payload.source: live measurement 2026-09-20/21 - Railway production deployment logs, Sentry, pg_stat_statements, EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) against the live database, and a warm/cold PostgREST probe with an order-reversed control
